question: A bullet train covers a fixed distance in 30 minutes at an average speed of 240 km/h. Due to track maintenance, it needs to be diverted, increasing the distance by 20%. If the train needs to arrive at its destination on time (i.e., in 30 minutes), what should its new average speed be in km/h?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the travel time remains constant (30 minutes) in both cases, Speed is directly proportional to Distance.

Because the distance increases by 20%, the required average speed must also increase by exactly 20%.

New Speed = 240 + (20% of 240)

New Speed = 240 + 48 = 288 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 288 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Average Speed (S₁) = 240 km/h

Initial Time (T₁) = 30 minutes = 0.5 hours

New Time (T₂) = 30 minutes = 0.5 hours

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 Initial Distance: 120 km
 Speed: 240 km/h | Time: 30 min
 
 
 New Distance: 144 km (+20%)
 New Speed: 288 km/h | Time: 30 min

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial Distance (D₁) = 240 × 0.5 = 120 km

⇒ The distance is increased by 20% due to track maintenance.

⇒ New Distance (D₂) = 120 + (20 ÷ 100) × 120

⇒ D₂ = 120 + 24 = 144 km

⇒ The train needs to arrive in the same exact time window.

⇒ New Time (T₂) = 0.5 hours

⇒ New Speed (S₂) = D₂ ÷ T₂

⇒ S₂ = 144 ÷ 0.5 = 288 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 288 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct and Inverse Proportionality

When **Time is constant**, Distance and Speed are directly proportional (S₁ ÷ S₂ = D₁ ÷ D₂). When **Distance is constant**, Time and Speed are inversely proportional.

Unit Conversions for Speed

To convert an object's speed from km/h to m/s, multiply it by 5 ÷ 18. To change m/s back to km/h, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.

Average Speed

Average Speed over an entire journey equals Total Distance ÷ Total Time. If two equal distances are traveled at speeds a and b, the Average Speed is 2ab ÷ (a + b).
